The test image shows the **underside of a soybean leaf** with numerous small, round, reddish-brown spots scattered across the surface. The spots range from pinpoint to ~2mm, appear slightly raised/pustule-like, with no obvious yellow halos. This pattern is consistent with soybean rust, bacterial pustule, or septoria brown spot.

**Analysis Summary:**

**Test image observations:**
- Underside of a soybean leaf (visible pubescence/hairs)
- Many very small (pinpoint to ~1-2mm), round, dark reddish-brown spots scattered across the leaf
- Leaf remains green — no yellowing or chlorosis
- Spots appear slightly raised/pustule-like
- Some clustering near the leaf margin

**Comparison with top candidates:**

| Disease | Match |
|---|---|
| **Bacterial_Pustule** | Very strong — reference top-right panel shows near-identical presentation: leaf underside held in hand, scattered small reddish-brown spots on green leaf, same scale and density |
| Soybean_rust | Reference shows tan/orange uredinia (lighter colored), often with visible central pore; test spots are darker |
| Septoria_brown_spot | More angular spots, associated with leaf yellowing and defoliation from lower canopy; test leaf is fully green |
| Frogeye_leaf_spot | Larger spots (~5-10mm) with gray centers and distinct reddish borders |

The Bacterial_Pustule reference collage (top-right quadrant) is essentially the same composition as the test image — same camera angle, same leaf underside view, same scattered tiny reddish-brown spots on a still-green leaf. The description matches: small raised spots especially on undersides of leaves that develop from light green to light-colored/brown, with distinguishing tiny tan bumps without openings.
